definitions.explanation: A style of handwriting in which letters are joined together in a flowing manner. Most commonly refers to cursive Latin alphabet writing, but can also refer to cursive styles of other scripts.

examples.japanese: {筆記体|ひっきたい}で{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}く。
examples.english: To write one's name in cursive.

examples.japanese: この{手紙|てがみ}は{筆記体|ひっきたい}で{書|か}かれていて{読|よ}みにくい。
examples.english: This letter is written in cursive and is hard to read.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{筆記体|ひっきたい}を{習|なら}わない{学校|がっこう}も{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Recently, more and more schools no longer teach cursive writing.

notes:
A compound of {筆記|ひっき} (writing) and {体|たい} (style/form). In Japanese education, {筆記体|ひっきたい} usually refers to cursive Latin alphabet writing, which was once widely taught in English classes but is now less common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {筆記体|ひっきたい}で{書|か}く: to write in cursive
- {筆記体|ひっきたい}が{読|よ}めない: cannot read cursive
- {筆記体|ひっきたい}の{練習|れんしゅう}: cursive writing practice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {活字体|かつじたい}: print style; block letters — the non-cursive counterpart
- {草書|そうしょ}: cursive-style kanji — the highly simplified, flowing style of writing kanji
- {行書|ぎょうしょ}: semi-cursive kanji — an intermediate style between block and cursive kanji
- ブロック{体|たい}: block letters — print-style alphabet writing
